request.spec:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now carry tags. I ran `bin/e2e` and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V55__claim_tags.sql`, adds a `tags` column to `claim`. It holds the cleaned-up tags, sorted and joined by commas, or nothing when there are none.
- It also adds a `sheet_tag` table that records every tag ever used on a sheet. A tag keeps its total on the sheet even after no claim carries it any more, as the request asked for every tag ever used. The sheet's history snapshots pick up the new table automatically.

**Server** (`ClaimService`, `ClaimController`, `Claim`, new `SheetTag` and `SheetTagRepository`)
- When a claim is added or edited, the typed tags are split on commas, trimmed, lower-cased, repeats dropped and sorted.
- Tags can only be changed when the claim can be edited (a draft). A refused edit changes nothing.
- `CLAIM_ADDED` gets ` tags=a,b` at the end of the line when there are tags, after `ref=` if a reference is also given.
- A claim split off another carries the original's tags.
- A new `GET /api/sheets/{id}/claims/tags` lists the tags used on the sheet.

**Front end**
- The claim form has a `claim-form-tags` field, and each claim row shows its tags in a `claim-tags` cell, like `a, b`.
- The totals section shows a per-tag table, `tag-<tag>-due-total`. Each figure adds up the dues of the claims that count in the sheet's due total and carry that tag, so a claim with two tags counts in both.
- Unlike the main due total, the tag totals don't drop the highest and lowest figures and aren't held to the sheet's cap. The tests pass with this, but the request didn't say which way to go.

One thing to be aware of: a tag ends up in the per-tag test id exactly as typed. A tag containing spaces, like "team x", gives `tag-team x-due-total`. That works, but such tags would make awkward test ids.
